newsitem.title: UK: UK's Blair says he too ready to use EU veto.
newsitem.headline: UK's Blair says he too ready to use EU veto.

text.p: Opposition leader Tony Blair said on Monday that his Labour was also prepared to use Britain's veto if the country became isolated in Europe.

Blair was speaking after Prime Minister John Major, on an election campaign tour of fishing ports in southwest England, threatened to block European Union business unless Britain's partners agree to reform the community's fishing policies.

As EU fisheries ministers met in Luxembourg to discuss plans for further deep cuts in fishing quotas, Major said he was prepared to veto the EU's long-running inter-governmental conference (IGC) when it concludes in Amsterdam in June.
Blair said his party had not ruled out holding up IGC business to get the right changes in fishing policies that were in Britain's interests.

"Let me make one thing absolutely clear to you," he told a BBC radio interviewer. "Where Britain's interests are at stake, we are perfectly prepared to be isolated. What we don't seek is a policy of perpetual isolation."

Attacking the government's handling of last year's European Union ban on British beef exports following the mad cow disease scare, Blair said: "What we don't want is vacuous sabre-rattling. What we need is success."
Blair said a Labour government was prepared to "take a very tough line" on fish with the EU.
He said that Britain's EU partners knew that when they were negotiating with British Conseravtive ministers, they were negotiating with a divided party.
Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind said that while Blair was promising to use Britain's EU veto if needed, the Labour leader had once promised never to be isolated in Europe.
"How can you trust someone who says one thing to the electorate during the election, which is totally different to what he said a year ago," Rifkind said.
Asked about the conduct of the campaign for the May 1 election, Blair promised to fight a positive campaign, rather than the "wholly negative" campaign being run by the Conservatives.
"We are fighting a positive campaign," Blair said. "They are engaging in a campaign of abuse, an unpleasant campaign that has nothing to say about the future of this country."
